Evidence of water, particle plumes discovered on asteroid Bennu: NASA

By:The Indian Express - 22 March,2019

Short Detail

Bennu is the target of NASA’s Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer. (Image: NASA)Source:The Indian Express

A NASA spacecraft, that will return a sample of a near-Earth asteroid named Bennu to Earth in 2023, has discovered plumes erupting from the cosmic body’s surface — among a numerous other findings including evidence of water-bearing minerals.

Bennu also revealed itself to be more rugged than expected, challenging the mission team to alter its flight and sample collection plans, due to the rough terrain.

Bennu is the target of NASA’s Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer (OSIRIS-REx) mission, which began orbiting the asteroid on December 31 last year. Bennu, which is only slightly wider than the height of the Empire State Building(New York), may contain unaltered material from the very beginning of our solar system.

NASA telescope spots a cosmic 'cannonball' hurtling through space

By:CNET - 21 March,2019

Short Detail

To make you more exciting this could take you from Kerala to Kashmir in aroud one second.

Scientists at NASA have discovered a Pulsar Zip which could travel upto 4 million km/h ie;5 times faster than your average pulsar. To make it even more exciting if we build a cannon from it amd shot it to East it will come and hit back you in probably 35 seconds hmm, talk about a super human strength.

A pulsar is the rapidly rotating, dense star left behind in the wake of a massive supernova explosion. Astronomers believe that the explosion can send the pulsar hurtling through space like a cannonball. This one, named PSR J0002+6216, was discovered using NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, which originally launched to space in 2008, and a suite of Earth-based radio telescopes known as the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array.

NASA's Fermi Satellite Clocks a 'Cannonball' Pulsar

J0002 currently lies about 6,500 light-years away in a constellation known as Cassiopeia, and 53 light-years away from the remnants of a huge stellar explosion known as CTB 1. That explosion took place around 10,000 years ago and resulted in a rapidly expanding bubble of gas that engulfed the pulsar.

Pulsars are super dense, rapidly spinning neutron stars left behind when a massive star explodes.

This crop-guzzling insect may cost Indian farmers billions, warns UN

By:Business Standard - 21 March,2019

Short Detail

A crop-guzzling insect called The Fall Armyworm pest which is being moved from it's native Americas to Asia which will be a treath to the farmers of India and Thailand costing Billion's of dollars in Loss,warned the UN food agency.

The Fall Armyworm pest's came to Asia o last summer.

"We are here today together because we share a growing sense of alarm but also to learn from each other, particularly from those countries who've already been responding to their own infestations," said Kundhavi Kadiresan, Assistant Director-General and FAO Regional Representative for Asia and the Pacific.

The flying pests (Fall Armywore) have already cost Africa a whopping $3Billion Dollar loss to it's farmers back in 2016.

In general,the pest lays egs which develop fast into grubs, which then can ruin crops such as maize, rice and sugarcane, overnight.

Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand and China's Yunnan are also being affected.Note:China's the second largest maize producer in the world after the United States.

India’s deepest shaft cave discovered in Meghalaya

By:Hindustan Times - 21 March,2019

Short Detail

Barely a year after the discovery of the world’s longest sandstone cave Krem Puri in Mawsynram region of Meghalaya’s East Khasi Hills district, now a cave with the deepest shaft in the country has been discovered.

Krem Umladaw, the cave with the deepest shaft in India. Photo Courtesy Marcel Dikstra, Netherlands,Source:Hindustan Times

The discovery was made during the 28th edition of the annual ‘Caving in the Abode of the Clouds Expedition’ that took place between February 3 and 28.

Krem Puri, which at 24,583 metres, is acknowledged as the longest sandstone cave in the world, has now been further extended by another 459 m to top the cave at 25,042 metres.

The main expedition team concentrated its efforts in the area of Muallian in East Jaintia Hills. From February 11 to 28 they explored and mapped 8 new caves including a revisit to Krem Shrieh (Tangnub). Krem Shrieh which was earlier explored in the year 2000 was now extended from 8,713m to 9,844m.

The other major caves explored and mapped are Retdung Khur 3724m, Tui Khur Lut 2185m and Kellung Puk 788m. Overall the 2019 expedition explored and mapped 12.3 kms of new cave passage.

Till date the whereabouts of about 1,700 caves and cave locations are known in Meghalaya of which over 1000 have been explored or partially explored.Source:Hindustan Times

Mizoram passes Bill for total prohibition

By:The Indian Express - 21 March,2019
Violation of the provisions could lead to imprisonment upto five years and a maximum fine of Rs 1 lakh. Source:The Indian Express

Short Detail

The Mizoram Assembly on Wednesday unanimously passed a Bill to implement total prohibition, a legislation promised by the Mizo National Front (MNF) government when it came to power last year.

Earlier this month, the state government had passed an order, saying that owners of liquor warehouses, vendors and those holding liquor licences in clubs, government lodgings or hotels should “dispose of all their stocks before March 31”.
